statement: Configuration is one aggregate per workspace: a compare-and-set chain of source CIDs, where a version takes effect only through a pure evaluation and, if it touches privilege, an approval in access. Applying it drives triggers, schedules, connections and channel shells through cross-context policies. Evidence and records sit beside every other context. Evidence holds the checkpoint chain, its external anchors, verification and exports. Records holds retention schedules, holds and per-subject erasure, and only ever acts by releasing or pinning content roots and shredding keys, never by deleting events.

event_changes.why: O2: a signature by the operator's own key proves nothing against the operator. The checkpoint must be recorded as published to an anchor outside the operator's control, after AuditLogCheckpointSigned.
Verifiers need the history of ledger keys. The new key is signed by the old one and the rotation is approved by an auditor, otherwise a stolen or replaced key cannot be detected.
AuditLogTamperDetected opens an incident and a cloud-wide preservation hold. Closing it needs a recorded finding by two people before that hold can be released.

hotspot_resolutions.resolution: The ledger signing key is a dedicated signatory for the cloud ledger, separate from package signatories. It lives in an HSM or OS keyring that the cloud process can ask to sign but cannot export, and never sits in the data directory beside secrets JSON or users.json. Every checkpoint (global position, chain head hash, previous checkpoint hash, key id) is anchored outside the operator's control in two places. The first is the hub, as an entry in a signed untethered stream for the cloud, reusing sequence, previous CID and signatory. The second is a public transparency log or an RFC 3161 timestamp authority. Auditors may also run their own witness that countersigns checkpoints. Verification is done by an independent verifier outside the cloud, which reads the export API and compares against the anchors, not against the cloud's own copy. A rewrite by an admin then shows up as a fork from an anchored head. Key rotation is CheckpointKeyRotated, signed by the old key and approved by an auditor. A lost key is treated as a tamper incident.

Four eyes (a PrivilegeChangeProposed followed by an approval from a different person) is required for the following. Access: AdminGranted, PersonShellAssigned, ChannelShellChanged and any WorkspaceSourceChanged whose evaluation changes a channel shell, person shell or admin. Shells are functions, so 'wider' cannot be decided in general; every change of shell CID needs approval except a move to a shell on the cloud's declared narrowing list (pure, read_only). Records: shortening a RetentionPolicySet, LegalHoldReleased and ShredSubjectKey outside a self-service request. Evidence: EventUpcasterRegistered, CheckpointKeyRotated and TamperIncidentResolved. An agent, trigger, schedule or connection may propose (on behalf of its principal), but may never approve, whatever its shell says. The approver must have actor kind person, have signed in recently, be someone other than the proposer, and not appear in the proposal's on_behalf_of chain. A cloud with a single admin cannot get a second person. There, self-approval is allowed only after a 24 hour cooling-off delay, is recorded as self-approved, and shows on the ledger health view until a second admin exists.

invariants: SetWorkspaceSource is compare-and-set on expected_previous_cid; a stale base is rejected, never merged silently
the source block is stored before the event that references it
every change carries a reason; a revert carries restores=<earlier source CID> that exists in this stream
at most one version is in force; Applied only for a source CID in this stream and only the latest source (a superseded pending version is rejected)
a version that changes privilege is not applied without a PrivilegeChangeApproved reference
Applied lists the secret names read, the evaluated config CID and the package pins used to evaluate
checkpoint positions strictly increase and each one commits to the previous checkpoint hash
the chain head hash equals the recomputed hash at that global position
signed only by the current key; a rotation is signed by the previous key
verification references an anchored checkpoint; a failed verification opens an incident that only TamperIncidentResolved closes
nothing in this stream is ever purged by retention
the scope is within the requester's audit grants
the export ends at an anchored checkpoint and includes raw events, upcaster CIDs and the checkpoint proofs
erased or purged payloads appear as tombstones, never as silent gaps
recipient and legal basis are mandatory
one upcaster per (event type, from version)
the upcaster is a pure EYG function by CID and passes its test vectors
approved by a second person
a period is never below the statutory minimum for its category; evidence and decision envelopes are kept indefinitely
shortening a period needs an approval reference
a purge cites the policy version it applied, releases only payload roots older than the period, and never touches roots pinned by a hold
a hold has a matter, a non-empty scope and a placing person or the tamper policy
released at most once, by a different approver from the requester
a preservation hold opened by tamper detection cannot be released while its incident is open
each request has a received time and a deadline
the key is shredded at most once per key version

a shred requires the active-holds view at a global position no earlier than the request; if a hold is placed afterwards, it lands on already-shredded data and the conflict is reported, not hidden (the cross-aggregate race is accepted and made visible)
a refusal names the holds that block it
